title: CODATA 2022: G is 6.674 30 × 10⁻¹¹, with a much larger relative uncertainty than h
summary: Newton's constant is not a defining constant. The 2022 listing gives 6.674 30 × 10⁻¹¹ m³ kg⁻¹ s⁻², standard uncertainty 0.000 15 × 10⁻¹¹.
body: The NIST 2022 complete listing prints 'Newtonian constant of gravitation 6.674 30 e-11' with standard uncertainty '0.000 15 e-11', unit m³ kg⁻¹ s⁻². That uncertainty is about 2 parts in 100,000 of the value. By contrast, the same listing marks the Planck constant and the speed of light as exact. G is not one of the seven defining constants on the BIPM page. A quoted G that pretends to be known as tightly as c is not what this table says.
